title: EtherCAT
summary: EtherCAT is a fast Ethernet fieldbus in which the frame passes through every device, which reads and writes its data on the fly.

sections.heading: Key ideas
sections.body: The master sends frames that travel through all slaves in a logical ring. Each slave runs a state machine (INIT, PRE-OPERATIONAL, SAFE-OPERATIONAL, OPERATIONAL). Distributed clocks synchronize devices for motion control. The working counter tells the master how many slaves processed the data.

sections.heading: Typical faults
sections.body: A slave stuck in PREOP or SAFEOP, wrong configuration (device revision), cable faults that break the ring at a given position, and working-counter errors.

sections.heading: In PLC Lab
sections.body: PLC Lab does not simulate this protocol. This article is background knowledge; no conformance or interoperability is claimed.
